---
title: "Lab 03 — Regression for description and prediction"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(tidyverse)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("../R/lab_submission.R")
world <- read_csv("data/country_indicators.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
fit <- lm(life_expectancy ~ gdp_per_capita, data = world)
lab_meta <- list(id = "lab03", title = "Regression for description and prediction")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "The slope of life expectancy on GDP per capita is an association of about…",
  q2 = "A fitted value is…",
  q3 = "Which use of the line is honest?",
  q4 = "Why is a prediction at a GDP far outside this sample risky?"
)
```

## What you will do

Read one OLS slope as description, not as an effect of a policy. Then download the `.txt`.

```{r coef-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=2}
coef(fit)
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("0.00018 years per extra dollar of GDP per capita (about 1.8 years per $10,000).", correct = TRUE),
  answer("71 years, regardless of GDP."),
  answer("r = 1, a perfect causal effect."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("The life expectancy the line predicts at a country's GDP.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The causal effect for that country."),
  answer("The residual."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("\"In this sample, higher GDP is associated with higher fitted life expectancy.\"", correct = TRUE),
  answer("\"The regression proves that raising GDP increases life expectancy.\""),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q4}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  open_answer(),
  trim = TRUE
)
```

## Submit

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = shiny::reactiveValuesToList(learnr::get_tutorial_state()),
      prompts = lab_prompts
    )
  }
)
```
